chunks: And from him, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Yūnus, from Ṭalḥah, who said:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام, “Indeed, the Imam is not washed except by the Imam.”
So he said, “Do you not know who was present for his washing? Those who attended it were better than those who were absent from it.”
Those who were present with Yūsuf in the well when his parents and his household were absent from him.”

key_terms.الْجُبِّ: the well into which Yūsuf عليه السلام was cast
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُ: washes him for the funeral rite

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain who washes the Imam after death?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the principle that an Imam is washed for burial only by an Imam, while indicating that the true reality of who attended such a washing may not be known to outward observers. It draws an analogy with Prophet Yūsuf عليه السلام in the well, where those physically present were not his closest family, showing that absence and presence may differ from what people assume.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Yunus, from Talha who said,
‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Imam<sup>asws</sup> is such that none can wash him<sup>asws</sup> (for funeral) except (another) Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What would make you know who was present for his<sup>asws</sup> washing? (The ones who) had attended it were better than those who were absent from it.
Those who attended Yusuf<sup>as</sup> in the well when his<sup>as</sup> parents and his<sup>as</sup> family were absent from him<sup>as</sup>’.
